h: Harry Potter Cloisters and a Hill to Climb
p: The Eastern Avenue retail park puts AirHop on the eastern side of Gloucester, which is handy for one of the city's best free outdoor spots. Robinswood Hill Country Park rises up just to the south, with woodland trails, open grassland and big views across the city and out towards the Malverns and the Forest of Dean. If the sun shows its face after your session, it's a great place to stretch legs that have gone a bit wobbly.

The cathedral is worth a proper look, and kids who've seen the Harry Potter films might recognise the cloisters, which were used as corridors of Hogwarts. It turns a bit of history into a game of spot-the-scene. Down at the docks, the National Waterways Museum tells the story of Britain's canals and sits among the old warehouses, and Gloucester Quays is right there for food and a mooch round the outlet shops.

Gloucester also has a lovely literary link: Beatrix Potter's The Tailor of Gloucester was inspired by a story she heard here, and the cathedral close is the setting she had in mind. Little readers might enjoy hunting for the spot.
Sports fans should know that Gloucester Rugby play at Kingsholm, and match days bring a real buzz to the city. Plan around the crowds if you're driving in.
And because the city is wedged between the Cotswolds and the Forest of Dean, a jump session here pairs easily with a bigger weekend of walks, villages and countryside on either side.
